risks: Baseline verification is red at the inspected clean revisions: Catalog, Orders, Notifications, and Gateway each report 0 passing and 1 failing test; the Coordinator public integration test also reports 0 passing and 1 failing test, first observing v1 instead of v2.

The public Notifications test covers only v2 acceptance and duplicate delivery; retained-v1 acceptance and malformed or unsupported rejection remain unverified by public tests and must still be implemented.

The orders-catalog slice spans two independently versioned repositories, so Catalog must be fully available before Orders publishes v2; Orders publication must also wait until the Notifications consumer rollout is complete.

The local repositories contain no production transport or checkout orchestrator. Cross-service propagation is represented only by the Coordinator public integration test, so real deployment and persistence behavior remain outside this bounded change.

assumptions: The authoritative retained v1 shape is the current flat Orders event: type, version, id, orderId, sku, and quantity.

Malformed means a missing or incorrectly typed required field for the selected version; quantity must be a positive integer, identifiers and locale/inventoryRevision must be non-empty strings, occurredAt must be a valid timestamp, and v2 order must be an object with id, sku, and quantity.
Adding inventoryRevision to a known-SKU Catalog response and eventVersion to the Gateway response are additive compatibility changes.

The Coordinator public integration test is the bounded end-to-end acceptance path and requires no writable Coordinator slice: it passes Catalog's inventoryRevision into Orders and then passes the resulting event to Notifications and Gateway.
No files were modified; implementation-time commits and HANDOFF records remain duties of the subsequent slice owners.
